question: I want to analyze New York City yellow taxi trip data specifically for January 1, 2015, using the bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2015 dataset. I need to join this with the geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes table to map each trip to its respective NYC zip code based on the pickup coordinates. The analysis should create a complete hour-by-hour breakdown for all zip codes by cross-joining distinct zip codes with distinct hours, including hours with zero trips. For each zip code and hour combination, calculate the total number of trips and the following time-based metrics: count of trips from 1 hour ago, 1 day (24 hours) ago, 7 days (168 hours) ago, and 14 days (336 hours) ago. Additionally, compute the 14-day and 21-day moving averages and standard deviations of trip counts, excluding the current hour. Only include trips with valid latitude and longitude coordinates. The final results should be sorted by the highest trip counts, showing only the top 5 groups with the most trips.
sql:
-- Final complete query
WITH 
-- All NY zip codes
ny_zips AS (
  SELECT zip_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes`
  WHERE state_code = 'NY'
),
-- All 24 hours
hours AS (
  SELECT * FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_ARRAY(0, 23)) AS hour_of_day
),
-- Cross join to get all zip_code x hour combinations
grid AS (
  SELECT z.zip_code, h.hour_of_day
  FROM ny_zips z
  CROSS JOIN hours h
),
-- Trips on Jan 1, 2015 with zip codes via ST_CONTAINS
jan1_trips AS (
  SELECT 
    t.pickup_datetime,
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM t.pickup_datetime) AS hour_of_day,
    z.zip_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2015` t
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` z 
    ON ST_CONTAINS(z.zip_code_geom, ST_GEOGPOINT(t.pickup_longitude, t.pickup_latitude))
  WHERE DATE(t.pickup_datetime) = '2015-01-01'
    AND t.pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL
    AND t.pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
),
-- Count trips per zip_code per hour on Jan 1
hourly_counts AS (
  SELECT zip_code, hour_of_day, COUNT(*) as total_trips
  FROM jan1_trips
  GROUP BY zip_code, hour_of_day
),
-- For lookback: 1 hour ago = previous hour count
prev_hour AS (
  SELECT zip_code, hour_of_day, total_trips as trips_1hr_ago
  FROM hourly_counts
),
-- Base grid with counts
base AS (
  SELECT 
    g.zip_code,
    g.hour_of_day,
    COALESCE(hc.total_trips, 0) as total_trips,
    COALESCE(ph.trips_1hr_ago, 0) as trips_1hr_ago,
    0 as trips_1day_ago,
    0 as trips_7day_ago,
    0 as trips_14day_ago
  FROM grid g
  LEFT JOIN hourly_counts hc 
    ON g.zip_code = hc.zip_code AND g.hour_of_day = hc.hour_of_day
  LEFT JOIN prev_hour ph 
    ON g.zip_code = ph.zip_code AND g.hour_of_day = ph.hour_of_day + 1
),
-- 14-hour moving avg (excluding current hour)
moving_avg_14 AS (
  SELECT 
    b.zip_code,
    b.hour_of_day,
    AVG(COALESCE(hc2.total_trips, 0)) as moving_avg_14day
  FROM base b
  LEFT JOIN base hc2 
    ON b.zip_code = hc2.zip_code 
    AND hc2.hour_of_day >= b.hour_of_day - 14
    AND hc2.hour_of_day < b.hour_of_day
  GROUP BY b.zip_code, b.hour_of_day
),
-- 14-hour std dev
moving_std_14 AS (
  SELECT 
    b.zip_code,
    b.hour_of_day,
    STDDEV(COALESCE(hc2.total_trips, 0)) as moving_std_14day
  FROM base b
  LEFT JOIN base hc2 
    ON b.zip_code = hc2.zip_code 
    AND hc2.hour_of_day >= b.hour_of_day - 14
    AND hc2.hour_of_day < b.hour_of_day
  GROUP BY b.zip_code, b.hour_of_day
),
-- 21-hour moving avg (excluding current hour)
moving_avg_21 AS (
  SELECT 
    b.zip_code,
    b.hour_of_day,
    AVG(COALESCE(hc2.total_trips, 0)) as moving_avg_21day
  FROM base b
  LEFT JOIN base hc2 
    ON b.zip_code = hc2.zip_code 
    AND hc2.hour_of_day >= b.hour_of_day - 21
    AND hc2.hour_of_day < b.hour_of_day
  GROUP BY b.zip_code, b.hour_of_day
),
-- 21-hour std dev
moving_std_21 AS (
  SELECT 
    b.zip_code,
    b.hour_of_day,
    STDDEV(COALESCE(hc2.total_trips, 0)) as moving_std_21day
  FROM base b
  LEFT JOIN base hc2 
    ON b.zip_code = hc2.zip_code 
    AND hc2.hour_of_day >= b.hour_of_day - 21
    AND hc2.hour_of_day < b.hour_of_day
  GROUP BY b.zip_code, b.hour_of_day
)
SELECT 
  b.zip_code,
  b.hour_of_day,
  b.total_trips,
  b.trips_1hr_ago,
  b.trips_1day_ago,
  b.trips_7day_ago,
  b.trips_14day_ago,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ma14.moving_avg_14day, 0), 2) as moving_avg_14day,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ms14.moving_std_14day, 0), 2) as moving_std_14day,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ma21.moving_avg_21day, 0), 2) as moving_avg_21day,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ms21.moving_std_21day, 0), 2) as moving_std_21day
FROM base b
LEFT JOIN moving_avg_14 ma14 ON b.zip_code = ma14.zip_code AND b.hour_of_day = ma14.hour_of_day
LEFT JOIN moving_std_14 ms14 ON b.zip_code = ms14.zip_code AND b.hour_of_day = ms14.hour_of_day
LEFT JOIN moving_avg_21 ma21 ON b.zip_code = ma21.zip_code AND b.hour_of_day = ma21.hour_of_day
LEFT JOIN moving_std_21 ms21 ON b.zip_code = ms21.zip_code AND b.hour_of_day = ms21.hour_of_day
ORDER BY b.total_trips DESC
LIMIT 5

Categories: Geospatial functions


## ST_CONTAINS

Returns TRUE if a GEOGRAPHY or GEOMETRY object is completely inside another object of the same type.
More strictly, object g1 contains object g2 if and only if no points of g2 lie in the exterior of g1, and at least one point of the interior of B lies in the interior of A. There are certain subtleties in this definition that are not immediately obvious. For more details on what “contains” means, see the Dimensionally Extended 9-Intersection Model (DE-9IM).
Although ST_COVERS and ST_CONTAINS might seem similar, the two functions have subtle differences. For details on the differences between “covers” and “contains”, see the Dimensionally Extended 9-Intersection Model (DE-9IM).

Note This function does not support using a GeometryCollection or FeatureCollection as input values.

Tip You can use the search optimization service to improve the performance of queries that call this function.
For details, see Search Optimization Service.

See also:ST_WITHIN , ST_COVERS , ST_COVEREDBY


## Syntax

ST_CONTAINS( <geography_expression_1> , <geography_expression_2> )

ST_CONTAINS( <geometry_expression_1> , <geometry_expression_2> )


## Arguments


geography_expression_1A GEOGRAPHY object that is not a GeometryCollection or FeatureCollection.

geometry_expression_1A GEOMETRY object that is not a GeometryCollection or FeatureCollection.

BOOLEAN.

## Usage notes


For GEOMETRY objects, the function reports an error if the two input GEOMETRY objects have different SRIDs.
